description: PER-TRACER lateral inflow for the regional monotone PPM stack on a limited-area latlon patch (12x9x4, lon [0,60], lat [20,60], no poles, no zonal wrap). Two tracers ride the SAME air-mass flux through the SAME lon/lat inflow rules, each binding its OWN prescribed Dirichlet halo to the rules' qbc_{w,e,s,n} PARAMS. Tracer A's halo is 1.0 on all four walls and matches its uniform interior q==1, so every CW84 correction is a difference of equal values, each open-wall flux collapses to F = M bitwise, and devA = mqA - m stays EXACTLY 0. Tracer B is identical except its WEST halo is 2.0; the west wind blows INTO the domain, so the mismatched halo is donated and devB departs zero. MEASURED (julia, Tsit5, reltol 1e-10 / abstol 1e-12): devA Linf = 0.0 exactly at t=0.1; devB Linf = 1.8742645277859651 at t=0.1. BOTH assertions are load-bearing and they fail in opposite directions. devA==0 pins that carrying the halo as a rule param left the scheme's free-stream property bitwise intact -- it is the same invariant latlon3d_transport_cwc_regional_inflow gates, re-checked in the two-tracer setting. devB's non-zero golden is the NON-VACUITY twin: it proves B's halo is actually READ and read INDEPENDENTLY of A's. This is the regression gate for qbc being a rule PARAM rather than a free name: were the halo a free name read from the consumer's scope, one model scope would hold exactly one `qbc_w`, both tracers would necessarily resolve it, devB would sit at 0.0 alongside devA, and this case would fail -- i.e. the document is unexpressible under the old contract, which is the point. A rule that silently ignored its halo operands would likewise pass devA and fail devB. Geometry, winds, metric and the initial mass profile are taken verbatim from problems/latlon3d_transport_cwc_regional_inflow.esm, so halo independence is the only new thing under test.
